2607.27767.title: Train Small, Deploy Large: Zero-Shot GNN Transfer Through Geometric Renormalization
2607.27767.paper_summary: Graph neural networks (GNNs) can operate on large graphs but become infrastructure-sensitive at the scale of millions of nodes and typically require scalable training techniques for even larger graphs. This raises a central question: when can a model trained on a smaller, scaled-down replica of a graph be deployed on the full-resolution graph without retraining? We introduce a zero-shot transfer protocol in which a GNN is trained on a graph coarse-grained by geometric renormalization (GR), and the resulting weights are transferred directly to the original network. Across synthetic and real-world networks, training on GR scaled-down replicas preserves much of the original-scale predictive performance while significantly reducing training cost. We further find that learned representations and predictive trajectories remain aligned across scales. These findings suggest that structural similarity may be more important than network size in determining GNN transferability, opening a path toward scale-equivariant graph architectures.
2607.27767.paper_summary_zh: 圖神經網絡（GNNs）可以在大型圖上運作，但在數百萬節點的規模下變得對基礎設施敏感，並且通常需要可擴展的訓練技術來處理更大的圖。這引發了一個核心問題：何時可以在不重新訓練的情況下，將在較小、縮小版本的圖上訓練的模型部署到全解析度的圖上？我們介紹了一種零樣本轉移協議，在該協議中，GNN在通過幾何重正化（GR）粗粒化的圖上進行訓練，並將得到的權重直接轉移到原始網絡上。在合成和現實世界的網絡中，在GR縮小版本上進行訓練保留了大部分原始規模的預測性能，同時顯著降低了訓練成本。我們進一步發現，學習到的表示和預測軌跡在不同尺度之間保持一致。這些發現表明，結構相似性在決定GNN可轉移性方面可能比網絡大小更為重要，為規模等變圖架構開啟了一條道路。
